name: RF Swift
what_it_is: RF Swift is a containerized RF testing toolbox that transforms any computer into a wireless assessment lab without requiring a dedicated OS. It provides 15+ specialized OCI images covering SDR, telecom (2G–5G), Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, RFID, automotive, hardware, and reversing, orchestrated via a Go CLI that wraps Docker, Podman, or Lima.
components: rfswift CLI (Go) — unified container lifecycle manager (run, exec, upgrade, profile, transfer, cleanup, doctor)
corebuild base image — Ubuntu Noble foundation shared by all derived images
sdrsa_devices image — SDR hardware drivers (UHD/USRP, RTL-SDR, HackRF, BladeRF, Airspy, LimeSDR, PlutoSDR, XTRX, RFNM, SoapySDR)
sdr_light image — GNU Radio + GQRX + SDR++ + SDRangel + SigDigger + CyberEther + Inspectrum + URH + rtl_433 + dump1090 + GNSS-SDR + SatDump + Jupyter + 50+ OOT modules
sdr_full image — superset of sdr_light with additional GNU Radio OOT modules
telecom_utils image — PySIM, pycrate, SigPloit, SCAT, jSS7, 5Greplay
telecom_2Gto3G image — YateBTS, OpenBTS, OsmoCom BTS Suite
bluetooth image — BlueZ, WHAD, Mirage, Sniffle, Bluing, bdaddr, ice9-bluetooth
wifi image — Aircrack-ng, hcxdumptool, Reaver, EAPHammer, Wifite2, Dragonslayer/Dragonforce/Wacker (WPA3), Hostapd-mana, Wifiphisher
rfid image — Proxmark3 (RRG/Iceman), libnfc, mfoc, mfcuk, RFIDler, miLazyCracker
automotive image — can-utils, CANtact, Caring Caribou, SavvyCAN, Gallia, V2GInjector
hardware image — PulseView, DSView, Logic 2 (Saleae), Arduino IDE, Flashrom, OpenOCD, esptool, openFPGALoader, ngscopeclient
reversing image — Ghidra, Radare2, Cutter, ImHex, Binwalk (v2+v3), Unblob, AFL, Honggfuzz, Semgrep, Joern, Qiling
network image — Nmap, Wireshark, Metasploit, Burp Suite, Caido, Impacket, NetExec, Responder, Hashcat, Kismet, Bettercap, SIPVicious
Lima VM layer — QEMU-backed VM for macOS USB passthrough via QMP hot-plug
YAML recipe engine — declarative build recipes (type: run / script / workdir / cleanup steps) for custom image composition
protocols: Bluetooth Classic + BLE (BlueZ, WHAD, Sniffle, ice9-bluetooth)
Wi-Fi 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax including WPA3 (Aircrack-ng, EAPHammer, Dragonslayer)
CAN bus / OBD-II (can-utils, SavvyCAN, Gallia, V2GInjector)
measurement: RF spectrum analysis via GNU Radio, GQRX, SDR++, SDRangel, SigDigger, CyberEther
Signal inspection and demodulation via Inspectrum and URH (Universal Radio Hacker)
Calibration via NanoVNASaver, NanoVNA-QT, LibreVNA, Leo Bodnar GPSDO (v1/v2), KCSDI calibrator
Jupyter notebook environment for interactive RF analysis and measurement
OpenCL GPU-accelerated signal processing (Intel and NVIDIA GPU images)
Network traffic capture via Wireshark, Kismet, SCAT (3GPP protocol logging)
Logic analyzer capture via PulseView, DSView, and Saleae Logic 2
Password/hash auditing benchmarks via Hashcat and John the Ripper
configuration: Container engine auto-detected at startup (Docker > Podman > Lima); overridable with --engine flag
YAML recipe files define base_image, labels, and ordered steps (run/script/workdir/cleanup) for custom builds
Container profiles (YAML presets) for quick deployment of preconfigured environments
Per-container settings: shell, X11 socket, XDISPLAY, PulseAudio server, seccomp profile, network mode, exposed/bound ports, ulimits, extra environment variables, extra hosts
Device passthrough via --devices flag; cgroup rules appended automatically for device access
Extra bind mounts via --extrabinding; workspace mount configurable or disabled
Privileged mode toggle (--privileged); Linux capabilities added à la carte (--caps)
Desktop (VNC/noVNC) mode configured via RFSWIFT_DESKTOP_* env vars (proto, host, port, pass, SSL)
NAT networking with configurable subnets for multi-container lab setups
Lima VM: 4 vCPU / 8 GiB RAM / 100 GiB disk defaults, adjustable in lima/rfswift.yaml
Podman rootless mode: cgroup v1/v2 auto-detected, device access rules configured automatically
macOS USB passthrough: rfswift macusb attach --vid <VID> --pid <PID> forwards USB to Lima QEMU VM via QMP
fault_injection: SigPloit — SS7/Diameter/GTP protocol-level attack and fuzzing against mobile core networks
jSS7 — SS7 stack attack toolkit (location tracking, call interception, SMS interception)
5Greplay — 5G NR traffic replay and modification for core network testing
EAPHammer — rogue AP / evil-twin attacks against WPA2-Enterprise (EAP) networks
Dragonslayer / Dragonforce / Wacker — WPA3 SAE Dragonblood vulnerability exploitation
Wifiphisher and Hostapd-mana — rogue AP phishing and credential capture
Reaver / Bully / Pixiewps — WPS PIN and Pixie Dust brute-force attacks
Airgeddon / Wifite2 — automated Wi-Fi attack orchestration
Caring Caribou — CAN bus diagnostic scanning and fuzzing (automotive ECU)
Gallia — automotive fuzzing framework targeting ECU services
AFL / Honggfuzz — coverage-guided fuzzing for binary firmware targets
Proxmark3 (RRG/Iceman) — RFID/NFC read, clone, emulate, and relay attacks
mfoc / mfcuk / miLazyCracker — MIFARE Classic cryptographic key recovery
gr-droneid — drone Remote ID signal analysis and potential spoofing research
gr-tempest — TEMPEST van Eck phreaking via SDR (EM side-channel)
modes: Interactive terminal mode — attach shell to running container (default)
Desktop mode — VNC or noVNC browser-based GUI inside container (--desktop flag with proto/port/pass)
Rootless Podman mode — daemonless, no root required, suitable for hardened/SOC-compliant environments
Lima macOS USB mode — QEMU VM with QMP hot-plug for SDR USB hardware on macOS (--engine lima)
Disconnected / air-gapped mode — pre-pulled images, no internet required at runtime
Multi-container NAT lab mode — isolated network subnet for interconnected container nodes
GPU-accelerated mode — OpenCL-enabled images for Intel or NVIDIA GPU signal processing
Session recording mode — built-in terminal session recording for documentation and audit
constraints: USB SDR hardware passthrough requires Linux (Docker or Podman) or macOS with Lima/QEMU; Docker Desktop on macOS cannot forward USB devices natively
Desktop (VNC/noVNC) mode requires the target image to include the desktop-start script and a VNC server; not all images ship this by default
Privileged mode or explicit device/cgroup rules are required for direct SDR hardware access inside containers; rootless Podman may need additional kernel configuration
YAML recipe builds require the entrypoint.sh script and all referenced function definitions to be present inside the image at build time
Lima VM for macOS USB is restricted to vmType: qemu — the Apple Virtualization Framework (vz) backend does not support USB passthrough
GPU OpenCL acceleration is only available in dedicated GPU-variant images and requires host OpenCL libraries and drivers to be accessible from the container
The image dependency graph is fixed (e.g., telecom_* images must be built on top of sdrsa_devices, not corebuild directly); custom recipes must respect the hierarchy
Windows and macOS hosts cannot use host network mode for containers; network-dependent tools (e.g., monitor mode Wi-Fi) require a Linux host or Lima VM
docker_services: penthertz/rfswift_noble:corebuild — Ubuntu Noble base with common build dependencies
penthertz/rfswift_noble:sdr_full — full SDR environment with all OOT modules
penthertz/rfswift_noble:telecom_2Gto3G — 2G/3G base station simulation and attack
penthertz/rfswift_noble:hardware — hardware hacking and logic analysis tools
penthertz/rfswift_noble:reversing — binary analysis and fuzzing tools
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository — containers are managed entirely via the rfswift CLI, not Compose
No built-in scoring, grading, or automated pass/fail test harness for RF assessments
No traffic generation or simulation tooling for realistic RF channel emulation (e.g., AWGN, fading channel models)
No dedicated SIM card provisioning or IMSI catcher detection tooling beyond what pycrate/PySIM provide
No built-in CI-driven regression tests for RF scenarios; CI pipeline (go.yml) only builds and releases the Go CLI binary
